tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: [BLOCKER] No route of administration, dose, dosing frequency, formulation, or PK/PD model exists anywhere in the platform, yet all 25 molecules are labelled "therapeutics" — I ran a case-insensitive, word-boundary grep for the full DMPK vocabulary across all four project files (README.md, app.js, index.html, styles.css). The following strings occur ZERO times: dose, doses, dosing, dosage, route, administered, administration, intravenous, subcutaneous, intrathecal, intranasal, infusion, injection, bolus, half-life, bioavailability, exposure, plasma, serum, CSF, cerebrospinal, microdialysis, Kp, Kp,uu, efflux, P-gp, MDR1, MDCK, BCRP, transcytosis, permeability, Papp, protease, peptidase, proteolysis, stability, aggregation, solubility, excipient, lyophil, hemolysis, anti-drug antibody. Every apparent hit is a substring artifact that I verified individually: "clearance" is always glutamate, lysosomal or autophagic clearance (README.md:89; app.js:64,65,112,333,359); "blood" is always "blood-brain barrier" or "cerebral blood flow" (app.js:34,116,118,119,349,356,373,376); "vial" comes from the FontAwesome class fa-flask-vial (index.html:35,89,117); "PK", "Vd", "ADA" and "oral" match inside amino-acid sequences and inside the JS identifier querySelectorAll. The per-drug modal (app.js:606-643) exposes exactly six numbered fields, and none of them is a route, a dose, a schedule, a vehicle, or an exposure. The word "therapeutic" appears 14 times across README.md, app.js and index.html. Consequence: A binding affinity without a delivery plan is not a drug candidate and cannot be triaged, prioritized, resourced or advanced. Any reader -- a collaborator, an investor, a grant reviewer, a student -- who takes README.md:45 ("We engineered 25 targeted bio-conjugate therapeutics") at face value will believe that a preclinical package exists. The consequence is concrete: the leaderboard at app.js:869-895 ranks candidates on pLDDT, dG and a "Cognitive Enhancement Index", so any decision made from this platform allocates effort purely on predicted potency, which is the single least predictive parameter for CNS success. In my experience the modal failure of CNS programs is not affinity, it is exposure at the target compartment; a platform that omits exposure entirely will systematically rank the wrong molecules first.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Required fix for DMPK-01: Add a mandatory seventh field to every record in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA (app.js:138-398) and to the modal renderer (app.js:606-643), named "Delivery & Exposure", containing five sub-fields: (1) intended route -- IV, SC, intrathecal, ICV, or intranasal; (2) a dose/dose-interval estimate with units, or the literal string "NOT ESTIMATED"; (3) a predicted Kp,uu,brain with an explicit credible interval; (4) predicted fu,plasma and predicted serum t1/2; (5) the resulting unbound-brain-concentration-versus-Kd target-engagement ratio. Where a value has not been computed, render "NOT ESTIMATED -- no delivery assessment performed" rather than omitting the field, so the gap is visible rather than invisible. Simultaneously, until a delivery strategy exists, change every occurrence of "therapeutic" and "drug" to "binder design" or "candidate binder" in README.md, index.html and app.js, and add a standing disclaimer to the README executive overview stating that no route, dose, formulation or PK/PD assessment has been performed.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Ground truth for DMPK-01: The free-drug hypothesis is the accepted foundation of CNS pharmacology: pharmacological response is driven by the unbound concentration at the target site, not by affinity and not by total tissue concentration. A survey of DMPK leadership at 18 major pharmaceutical companies (Loryan et al., Pharm Res 2022;39:1321-1341, PMID 35411506) found 93% share a common cross-disciplinary understanding of Kp,uu,brain and 79% describe its adoption as "game-changing" for their CNS portfolios. A minimally credible candidate record must therefore carry, at absolute minimum: intended route; a dose or dose range with units; a dosing interval; the vehicle/formulation; predicted or measured fu,plasma and fu,brain; a predicted Kp,uu,brain; and a target-engagement calculation linking dose to unbound brain concentration versus Kd.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: [BLOCKER] All 25 candidates are 2.9-5.4 kDa hydrophilic polypeptides with no BBB transport moiety; their computed physicochemistry places CNS parenchymal exposure at or below that of an unmodified IgG, which is 0.028-0.07 %ID/g — I parsed all 25 sequences directly out of app.js and computed their properties (average residue masses, EMBOSS pKa set for charge and pI, Kyte-Doolittle for GRAVY, backbone NH plus side-chain donors for H-bond donor count). Results: length 26-47 residues (median 35); MW 2877-5436 Da (median 4094 Da); net charge at pH 7.4 spanning -7.20 to +8.93; isoelectric point 3.44-10.95; GRAVY -1.12 to +0.26 with a median of -0.92, i.e. 24 of 25 are net hydrophilic; hydrogen-bond donors 52-106 (median 80). Selected rows -- HippoTrk-Saponin-X1 (app.js:143): 47 aa, 5340 Da, q -0.54, GRAVY -0.94, 106 HBD. HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 (app.js:153): 36 aa, 4943 Da, q +8.93, pI 10.95, GRAVY -1.09, 36.1% Arg+Lys. MicroAutophagy-Tag-M4 (app.js:329): 32 aa, 4314 Da, q +6.93, 34.4% Arg+Lys. HippoNrf-KeapDecoy-X3 (app.js:163): 28 aa, 3508 Da, q -7.20, pI 3.44. Not one of the 25 carries a receptor-mediated-transcytosis shuttle, a TfR1 or CD98hc binder, an Fc, a glucose- or LAT1-transporter ligand, or any other BBB-crossing element; the conjugated "warheads" are natural products (ginsenosides, salvianolic acid B, curcumin) which are themselves notoriously poor CNS penetrants. The platform nevertheless states a parenchymal, cell-type-resolved destination for every one of them ("CNS -> Brain -> Hippocampus (CA1/CA3 Pyramidal Neurons & DG SGZ Neural Stem Cells)", app.js:145). Consequence: The central claim of the platform -- 25 therapeutics acting on five named brain regions -- requires the molecules to reach brain parenchyma. On the computed physicochemistry they will not, absent a delivery vehicle that does not exist in these designs. I ran the dose arithmetic for HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 using the platform's own claimed Kd of 2.1 nM (app.js:156), targeting 3xKd unbound brain concentration for ~75% occupancy, with Vd 0.1 L/kg, fu,plasma 0.05 and the predicted 27-min serum half-life: the required continuous-infusion dose for a 70 kg human is 16 g/day at Kp,uu 0.01 and 161 g/day at Kp,uu 0.001 (IgG-like). Under deliberately, implausibly generous assumptions (t1/2 4 h, Vd 0.3 L/kg, fu 0.5, Kp,uu 0.05 -- better than most successful CNS small molecules) it falls to 0.11 g/day. The dose requirement therefore swings by more than three orders of magnitude across parameters the platform never estimates and gives the reader no way to estimate. That is the harm: not that the answer is definitely "impossible", but that the platform presents these as finished therapeutics while withholding the one calculation that determines whether they are feasible or absurd.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Required fix for DMPK-02: Two changes. (a) Stop asserting parenchymal destinations that the molecules cannot reach: revise every "targets" field in FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA (app.js:145,155,165,...) to state the intended target compartment together with the delivery mechanism required to reach it, e.g. "Hippocampal CA1 pyramidal neurons -- REQUIRES a BBB delivery vehicle; none present in this design". (b) Attach an explicit delivery strategy per candidate, chosen from the real state of the art and named in the record: TfR1 receptor-mediated transcytosis (ATV:TfR-style Fc fusion, or Brainshuttle-style monovalent scFab), CD98hc RMT, intrathecal or ICV administration, focused-ultrasound-assisted delivery, or TfR1-retargeted AAV for a genetically encodable payload. For each, state the expected fold-enhancement over unmodified molecule with a citation. Add a computed properties panel to every card showing length, MW, net charge at pH 7.4, pI, GRAVY and HBD count -- these take ten lines of JavaScript and immediately expose to the reader why a shuttle is mandatory.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Ground truth for DMPK-02: Empirical CNS penetration limits for passive transcellular diffusion sit near 400-500 Da with roughly 8-10 hydrogen-bond donors; all 25 candidates exceed the MW ceiling by ~6-13x and the donor limit by ~5-13x. For large molecules the measured reality is stark: unmodified therapeutic IgG brain uptake is 0.07 %ID/g for the murine precursor of bapineuzumab and 0.028 %ID/g for mAb158 in mouse, and IgG in primate brain is <0.01% of the plasma concentration (Pardridge, Front Drug Deliv 2023;3:1227816, PMID 37583474, DOI 10.3389/fddev.2023.1227816). Pardridge (Pharmaceuticals 2020;13:394, PMID 33207605) states that 98% of small-molecule drugs and ~100% of biologic drugs do not cross the BBB. Engineered receptor-mediated transcytosis is what changes this: the Denali Fc-based transport vehicle binding the apical domain of human TfR1 produced "substantially improved CNS uptake and sustained pharmacodynamic responses" in hTfR-knockin mice and cynomolgus monkeys (Kariolis et al., Sci Transl Med 2020;12:eaay1359, PMID 32461332); Roche's Brainshuttle fusion trontinemab achieved a modelled 4-18-fold increase in brain exposure over gantenerumab in non-human primates at half the dose (Grimm et al., mAbs 2023;15:2261509, PMID 37823690); anti-CD98hc antibodies showed robust brain accumulation and a significant Abeta pharmacodynamic response (Zuchero et al., Neuron 2016;89:70-82, PMID 26687840). Alternative routes that bypass the BBB entirely -- intrathecal/ICV -- are the established path for CNS oligonucleotides and enzymes; focused-ultrasound BBB opening is now clinically demonstrated with an antibody payload (Rezai et al., N Engl J Med 2024;390:55-62, PMID 38169490); and TfR1-retargeted AAV capsids give 40-50x greater CNS expression than AAV9 in human-TfR1 knockin mice (Huang et al., Science 2024;384:1220-1227, PMID 38753766).

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: [CRITICAL] Four candidates are cationic amphipathic alpha-helices with hydrophobic moments exceeding LL-37 and pexiganan; the platform declares them "0% Cardiotoxicity" and "Tolerance Rate: 0.0%" and never assesses hemolysis or infusion reactions — I computed the Eisenberg consensus-scale hydrophobic moment over a sliding 18-residue, 100-degree-per-residue window for all 25 sequences, and calibrated against known membranolytic peptides on the identical scale and window. Results: X2/B1 muH = 0.89 at net charge +8.93 (36.1% Arg+Lys); M4 muH = 0.88 at +6.93 (34.4% Arg+Lys); X5 muH = 0.88 at +4.79 (27.3% Arg+Lys). Calibration on the same code: melittin (bee venom, hemolytic) 0.55; the (KLAKLAK)2 lytic peptide 0.69; pexiganan/MSI-78 0.75; LL-37 core 0.78; an idealized Leu/Lys amphipathic helix 0.63; polyalanine control 0.00. The four candidates therefore sit above every membranolytic reference I tested. The maximally amphipathic window in X2/B1 is KWWKFLRRFWRRLKKYFE -- a Trp/Phe-rich hydrophobic face opposed to an Arg/Lys polar face, which is the canonical pore-forming architecture. Against this, the platform asserts "0% Cardiotoxicity" and "Peripheral Side Effects: None" and the README (line 99) offers the affirmatively wrong mechanistic rationale that "hydrophobic peptide linkers sterically prevent binding to hERG pore Tyr652/Phe656" -- hydrophobicity in a cationic amphipath is the driver of membrane interaction, not a shield against it. There is no hemolysis assay, no HC50, no mast-cell degranulation or MRGPRX2 assessment, no infusion-reaction risk statement, and no complement-activation-related pseudoallergy consideration anywhere in the codebase. Consequence: Hemolysis and infusion reactions are the historical killers of this exact molecular class and they occur at concentrations in the range these designs would require. Typical HC50 (50% hemolysis) for cationic amphipathic alpha-helical peptides is roughly 5-100 uM. My dose arithmetic for X2/B1 (Vd 0.1 L/kg, fu 0.05, predicted t1/2 27 min, 3xKd target occupancy) gives a required total plasma concentration of 12.6 uM at Kp,uu 0.01 and 126 uM at Kp,uu 0.001 -- squarely inside and then far above the hemolytic window. A reader who trusts "Seizure Index: 0.01, Peripheral Side Effects: None, Tolerance Rate: 0.0%" would conclude that the principal safety liability of the molecule has been evaluated and cleared. It has not been evaluated at all, and the one liability that actually dominates this chemotype is the one liability the safety string does not mention. Stating a numeric "0%" risk for an unassessed hazard is worse than silence: it converts an absence of data into a false negative.

text: Required fix for DMPK-03: First, delete the fabricated numeric safety strings for these four candidates and every other candidate (app.js:147,157,167,177,187,199,209,219,229,239,251,261,271,281,291,303,313,323,333,343,355,365,375,385,395) and replace with "NOT ASSESSED". Second, add a computed-liability flag to each card: display net charge at pH 7.4, %Arg+Lys, and the Eisenberg hydrophobic moment, and raise an explicit "CATIONIC AMPHIPATHIC -- MEMBRANOLYTIC / HEMOLYSIS RISK" warning whenever muH > 0.5 and net charge > +3. Third, correct README.md:99, which currently states a mechanistically backwards rationale; replace with an honest statement that hERG liability has not been assessed and that hemolysis, not hERG, is the leading cardiovascular/haematological concern for cationic amphipathic peptides. Fourth, if these four candidates are to be retained, specify the required de-risking experiments: human RBC HC50, therapeutic index versus the required plasma Cmax, and MRGPRX2 activation.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Ground truth for DMPK-03: Membrane-lytic activity of alpha-helical peptides is governed by the combination of cationic charge and hydrophobic moment. Wieprecht et al. (Biochemistry 1997;36:6124-6132, PMID 9166783, DOI 10.1021/bi9619987) showed with magainin-2 amide analogues holding hydrophobic moment, charge and hydrophilic angle constant that increasing hydrophobicity drives permeabilization of zwitterionic PC-rich (i.e. mammalian) membranes and that "the antibacterial and hemolytic activity of the peptides increases with enhanced hydrophobicity", with a strong correlation between the hemolytic effect and PC-vesicle permeabilization. Maturana et al. (Colloids Surf B Biointerfaces 2017;153:152-159, PMID 28236791, DOI 10.1016/j.colsurfb.2017.02.003) showed with designed analogues differing in hydrophobic moment and net charge that affinity for zwitterionic rather than anionic membranes is what converts an antimicrobial into a hemolytic peptide. The correct developability panel for a cationic amphipath is: human erythrocyte HC50, a therapeutic index (HC50 divided by required plasma concentration), mammalian cell LDH release, MRGPRX2/mast-cell degranulation, and complement activation.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: [CRITICAL] Two candidates contain the amyloid-beta(16-35) core sequence verbatim and are proposed as systemically delivered anti-fibril agents with "Fibril Blockade: 100%" and no aggregation, seeding, immunogenicity or ARIA assessment — I retrieved the canonical human APP sequence from UniProt P05067 and mapped the fragment computationally. The string KLVFFAEDVGSNKGAIIGLM at app.js:277 and app.js:129 is an exact, contiguous match to Abeta residues 16-35 -- it begins at Lys16 with the KLVFF central hydrophobic cluster (Abeta 16-20) and runs through GAIIGLM (Abeta 29-35), i.e. it spans both hydrophobic segments that drive Abeta beta-sheet nucleation and fibril elongation. This is the amyloidogenic core of the peptide, not an inert epitope. Consistent with that, it is the only one of the 25 candidates with a positive GRAVY score (+0.26; every other candidate is between -0.30 and -1.12), which is the computational signature of its aggregation propensity. The platform proposes it as a systemically administered agent to a basal-forebrain target in an explicitly Alzheimer's-framed program and asserts "Fibril Blockade: 100%". There is no aggregation-propensity assessment, no thioflavin-T or seeding assay, no solubility or formulation statement, no immunogenicity assessment (only the unsupported label "Immunogenicity: Low" elsewhere in the file), and no consideration of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities. Consequence: Administering the amyloidogenic core of Abeta to a patient with cerebral amyloid pathology inverts the intended pharmacology: the KLVFF motif is the recognition element by which Abeta monomers self-associate, so an exogenous Abeta(16-35) peptide is a candidate seed and cross-seeder, not a self-evident inhibitor. Short KLVFF-based beta-sheet breakers exist in the literature, but they are deliberately truncated and chemically modified (N-methylated, D-amino-acid, or C-terminally disrupted) precisely to abolish self-assembly; extending to residue 35 restores the full nucleating unit. Separately and independently of any in-vivo seeding question, this is a formulation dead end: a 35-mer with a positive GRAVY and the Abeta hydrophobic core will aggregate in the vial, which is why the absence of any solubility/stability statement matters. And aggregated peptide is the single strongest driver of anti-drug-antibody formation, which the "Immunogenicity: Low" labels elsewhere in the file assert away without data. A reader seeing "Fibril Blockade: 100%" alongside "Seizure Index: 0.01" will conclude the safety case is closed on a molecule whose principal hazard has not been examined.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Required fix for DMPK-04: Truncate the fragment to the minimal recognition motif and chemically block self-assembly (N-methylation of the KLVFF backbone or D-residue substitution), or remove the candidate. In either case: delete the "Fibril Blockade: 100%" string at app.js:281 -- it is an unmeasured absolute; add an aggregation-propensity computation (e.g. a TANGO/AGGRESCAN-style or Waltz-style predictor) to every card and flag this candidate explicitly; add explicit fields for predicted solubility, oligomer content and immunogenicity risk with "NOT ASSESSED" where no data exists; and add a prominent note wherever this candidate appears (app.js:277 and app.js:129) stating that the sequence is Abeta(16-35) verbatim and that seeding and cross-seeding must be excluded experimentally before any therapeutic framing.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Ground truth for DMPK-04: Abeta(16-35) contains both the central hydrophobic cluster KLVFF (Abeta 16-20) and the C-terminal hydrophobic region, and is the canonical self-assembly-competent fragment; verified here by exact string match against UniProt P05067 residues 687-706 (Abeta 16-35). Correct practice for a beta-sheet-breaker design is to take the minimal recognition motif (typically KLVFF or LPFFD-type analogues), abolish its own aggregation competence by backbone N-methylation, D-amino-acid substitution or proline insertion, and then demonstrate absence of self-aggregation and absence of seeding before any in-vivo claim. Required assays: thioflavin-T kinetics for self-aggregation and for seeding of wild-type Abeta42; size-exclusion and dynamic light scattering for oligomer content in the formulated drug product; and, given the class, an explicit ARIA risk statement.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: [CRITICAL] Brain-region-specific targeting is asserted for all 25 candidates with no targeting mechanism, and is provably arbitrary: four pairs of byte-identical sequences are assigned to different brain regions with different Kd and different pLDDT — The platform's organizing claim is that 25 molecules are targeted to five distinct brain regions and cell types, five per region. I extracted all 25 sequences programmatically and found four pairs that are byte-identical yet carry contradictory downstream metadata. Pair 1: the same 36-mer is HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 with "Kd = 2.1 nM | AF3 pLDDT = 94.8" targeted to "Hippocampus (CA1 Cholinergic Terminals & Synaptic Cleft)", and simultaneously BasalAChE-GorgeBlock-B1 with "Kd = 0.65 nM | AF3 pLDDT = 94.3" targeted to "Basal Forebrain (Nucleus Basalis of Meynert NBM)" -- a 3.2-fold Kd difference and a different pLDDT for a structure prediction on an identical input string, which is not possible for a deterministic model. Pair 2: the same 31-mer is both a Frizzled-8 agonist in the dentate gyrus SGZ (Kd 1.2 nM, pLDDT 95.1) and a ZO-1 tight-junction protector at the BBB endothelium (Kd 2.8 nM, pLDDT 93.8). Pair 3: the same 41-mer is both an alpha7 nAChR PAM in PFC layer III/V (Kd 1.8 nM) and a TLR4/MD-2 antagonist on microglia (Kd 3.8 nM). Pair 4: the same 37-mer is both a TrkB ERK enhancer in PFC layer V (Kd 0.85 nM) and an astrocytic EAAT2 upregulator (Kd 3.6 nM). Separately, no candidate carries any element capable of producing regional or cell-type selectivity within brain parenchyma -- no cell-type-restricted receptor ligand, no capsid, no promoter, no locally activated prodrug. Consequence: This is the finding that most directly undermines the platform's headline. "25 therapeutics across 5 brain regions" reduces to at most 21 distinct sequences, four of which have been duplicated and relabelled, with the affinity and confidence numbers adjusted to fit the new label. Since affinity and pLDDT are functions of the molecule and its target, and the molecule is identical, at least one number in each pair must be fabricated -- and because the pLDDT differs too, the numbers cannot both come from the same prediction run. More fundamentally for delivery: even if every molecule crossed the BBB perfectly, regional selectivity within parenchyma does not arise from the peptide sequence alone. A soluble peptide entering brain interstitial fluid distributes by diffusion and bulk flow; it goes where the vasculature and the ISF take it, modulated only by target-mediated binding. Claiming that one molecule is a hippocampal CA1 drug and the byte-identical molecule is a nucleus basalis drug asserts a spatial selectivity that no mechanism in the design can deliver. Anyone using this platform to plan a target-engagement or biodistribution study would design the wrong study.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Required fix for DMPK-05: Deduplicate FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA: the four repeated sequences must either be collapsed into single entries or genuinely re-engineered so the sequences differ, and the conflicting Kd and pLDDT values must be removed since at most one value per pair can be correct. Add an automated uniqueness assertion at load time that throws if two records share a sequence. Then, for every record, replace the aspirational "targets" string with two explicit fields: "intended site of action" and "mechanism conferring selectivity for that site", where the second field must read "NONE -- distribution will be governed by ISF diffusion and target-mediated binding" unless a real mechanism (restricted receptor with cited expression data, vector tropism, or spatially localized delivery) is supplied. Finally, revise README.md:43-92 to state the actual number of distinct sequences.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Ground truth for DMPK-05: Regional and cell-type selectivity in CNS therapeutics comes from one of a small number of real mechanisms, none of which is present here: (i) a cell-type-restricted receptor with genuinely restricted expression, verified by proteomics rather than asserted; (ii) a delivery vector with intrinsic tropism -- for example the TfR1-retargeted AAV capsid BI-hTFR1, which gave CNS-specific enhanced tropism 40-50x over AAV9 in human-TfR1 knockin mice and no enhancement in wild-type mice (Huang et al., Science 2024;384:1220-1227, PMID 38753766, DOI 10.1126/science.adm8386); (iii) cell-type-restricted transcriptional control in a gene-therapy payload; or (iv) spatially localized delivery, such as focused-ultrasound BBB opening applied to selected regions, which produced numerically greater regional Abeta reduction in insonated versus contralateral homologous regions (Rezai et al., N Engl J Med 2024;390:55-62, PMID 38169490, DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa2308719). Distribution of a freely diffusing peptide in brain ISF is governed by diffusion, bulk flow and target binding, not by the designer's intent.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: [MAJOR] No proteolytic stability or plasma-half-life consideration; all 25 are unmodified linear L-peptides with free termini, predicted median human-serum t1/2 of 26 minutes — Every one of the 25 designs is an unmodified linear peptide of standard L-amino acids with a free N-terminus and free C-terminus. None is cyclized, none is N-methylated, none contains D-residues or beta-amino acids, none carries a PEG, an albumin-binding moiety, a lipid, or an Fc. The chemStruct fields describe only how the natural-product warhead is attached; there is no half-life-extension strategy anywhere. I applied the published Cavaco et al. human-serum half-life regression model (ln t1/2 = 2.226 + 0.053*NP% - 1.515*[Trp present] + 1.290*[>=2 Tyr] - 1.052*[pI >= 10]) to all 24 parseable sequences: predicted t1/2 ranges from 8 min (HippoDual-TrkB-AMPK-X5) to 100 min (AstroSuper-CBF-EAAT2-A5), median 26 min; 18 of 24 fall below 60 min and 24 of 24 below 120 min. Twenty-two of the 24 contain tryptophan, which the model identifies as the single largest destabilizing term, and four have pI >= 10, which is the second destabilizing term. The platform reports "Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days" (README.md:102) and "Tolerance Rate: 0.0%" (app.js:157) -- 30-day pharmacology assertions for molecules with a predicted plasma residence of tens of minutes and no stated dosing regimen. Consequence: Plasma half-life is the parameter that converts a required concentration into a required dose, and its absence is why the dosing arithmetic for these candidates is unbounded. For HippoAChE-AlkaPept-X2 with a predicted 27-min t1/2, Vd 0.1 L/kg and fu 0.05, sustaining 3xKd unbound brain concentration requires 16 g/day of synthetic peptide by continuous infusion at Kp,uu 0.01, versus 0.11 g/day under implausibly generous assumptions (t1/2 4 h, Vd 0.3, fu 0.5, Kp,uu 0.05). Approved synthetic peptide drugs are dosed in the range of roughly 0.001-10 mg/kg/day. A three-order-of-magnitude uncertainty that straddles the boundary between a manufacturable drug and a physical impossibility is not a detail; it is the go/no-go decision, and the platform provides no basis for making it. Separately, the "< 4.2% downregulation after 30 days" claim implies chronic sustained receptor occupancy that a minutes-scale half-life cannot produce under any plausible schedule.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Required fix for DMPK-06: Add a predicted-serum-half-life field to every record, computed from the sequence with a cited model (the Cavaco regression is a reasonable, transparent starting point) and displayed with an explicit uncertainty range, not a point estimate. Add a paired "half-life extension strategy" field, populated with the specific modification proposed (N/C-terminal capping, head-to-tail or disulfide cyclization, D-residue or N-methyl substitution at identified cleavage sites, lipidation, PEG, albumin binder, or Fc fusion) or "NONE". Add an explicit dose-projection panel per candidate that propagates predicted t1/2, assumed Vd, assumed fu,plasma and a predicted Kp,uu range through to a required dose with its full uncertainty interval, so the reader sees the three-order-of-magnitude spread rather than a false precision. Finally, delete README.md:102 and app.js:157 ("Tolerance Downregulation < 4.2% after 30 days", "Tolerance Rate: 0.0%") -- these are 30-day claims with no dosing regimen behind them.

text: Ground truth for DMPK-06: Cavaco et al. (Clin Transl Sci 2021;14:1349-1358, PMID 33641212, DOI 10.1111/cts.12985) curated 579 literature entries on peptide proteolytic lifetime and derived and validated a serum-t1/2 regression from unmodified peptides; their synthesized validation library spanned 7.4 to 403.4 minutes in human serum, with most peptides in the 30-60 min range. Unmodified linear peptides are cleaved by plasma aminopeptidases and carboxypeptidases from the free termini, by DPP-4 at position 2, and by neprilysin at hydrophobic residues, and are simultaneously cleared by glomerular filtration (a 3-5 kDa peptide is well below the ~60 kDa filtration threshold). Lau and Dunn (Bioorg Med Chem 2018;26:2700-2707, PMID 28720325, DOI 10.1016/j.bmc.2017.06.052) survey the >60 approved peptide drugs and the medicinal-chemistry strategies that made them viable: cyclization, N-methylation, D-amino-acid substitution, terminal capping, lipidation, PEGylation, and albumin or Fc fusion.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: [MAJOR] Efficacy is ranked on binding free energy and Kd alone; Kp,uu,brain, fu,plasma, fu,brain and MDCK-MDR1 efflux ratio -- the actual determinants of CNS effect -- appear nowhere, and the reported dG and Kd values are mutually inconsistent by 3-4 orders of magnitude — The platform's entire prioritization logic runs on affinity and structural confidence. The leaderboard (app.js:869-895) and the benchmark chart (app.js:1049-1103) rank candidates on pLDDT, dG and an undefined "Cognitive Enhancement Index"; not one exposure parameter enters the ranking. There is no unbound brain-to-plasma partition coefficient, no plasma or brain unbound fraction, no efflux-transporter assessment, and no in-vitro permeability estimate anywhere in the codebase. Secondarily, the two affinity numbers reported for each candidate are not consistent with one another: at 298 K, dG = -18.4 kcal/mol (app.js:146) corresponds to Kd = 3.2e-5 nM, not the stated 0.32 nM -- a factor of ~9,900. Across five spot-checked records the discrepancy ranges from 670x to 15,800x, always in the direction of the stated Kd being weaker than the stated dG implies, which indicates the two numbers were assigned independently rather than derived from one another. Consequence: Ranking CNS candidates on affinity is the classic way to advance the wrong molecule. Two candidates differing tenfold in Kd but hundredfold in Kp,uu,brain will have opposite efficacy orderings, and this platform would rank them backwards with full confidence. Because affinity is the only input, the leaderboard at app.js:869-895 is not merely incomplete -- it is actively anti-correlated with the property that matters for polar, high-molecular-weight polypeptides, where the exposure term dominates by orders of magnitude and the affinity term barely moves. The dG/Kd inconsistency compounds this: since Kd is the quantity that feeds any target-engagement or dose calculation, and it disagrees with the reported dG by up to four orders of magnitude, no dose can be derived from the platform's own numbers even in principle.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Required fix for DMPK-07: Replace the affinity-only leaderboard ranking (app.js:869-895) with a composite that requires an exposure term, and refuse to rank any candidate for which Kp,uu,brain has not been estimated -- show it as unranked rather than assigning it a position. Add to every record: predicted Kp,uu,brain with a credible interval, predicted fu,plasma, predicted fu,brain, predicted MDCK-MDR1 efflux ratio, and predicted Papp, each with an explicit applicability-domain flag for out-of-range molecules. Every one of these should be rendered as an interval, and where the model does not apply to a 4 kDa polypeptide, render "OUT OF DOMAIN" rather than a number. Separately, fix the dG/Kd inconsistency: derive one from the other with the stated temperature (Kd = exp(dG/RT), RT = 0.5924 kcal/mol at 298 K) and display the temperature, or remove one of the two quantities. Finally, define "Cognitive Enhancement Index" or remove it -- it is currently an undefined score driving a chart at app.js:1063 and a leaderboard column at index.html:306.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Ground truth for DMPK-07: The correct efficacy metric for CNS drugs is the unbound brain concentration relative to target potency, which requires Kp,uu,brain = Cu,brain / Cu,plasma -- not total brain concentration, which is confounded by nonspecific lipid and tissue binding and is the single most common error in CNS DMPK. Loryan et al. (Pharm Res 2022;39:1321-1341, PMID 35411506, DOI 10.1007/s11095-022-03246-6) surveyed European and US pharma and report that 93% have established a common cross-disciplinary understanding of Kp,uu,brain and 79% describe its implementation as "game-changing" for their portfolios; the paper also documents the accepted toolbox. The minimum honest in-silico DMPK layer for a platform like this is: (1) predicted Kp,uu,brain reported as a distribution or credible interval, never a point estimate; (2) predicted fu,plasma, with an explicit note that polycations bind albumin, alpha-1-acid glycoprotein and glycosaminoglycans; (3) predicted fu,brain from a brain-homogenate binding model; (4) an MDCK-MDR1 bidirectional efflux ratio, with ER > 2-2.5 flagged as P-gp-substrate risk, plus a BCRP assessment; (5) predicted passive permeability (Papp); and (6) a propagated target-engagement calculation from dose to Cu,brain/Kd carrying all upstream uncertainty. For a 3-5 kDa hydrophilic polypeptide, several of these predictors are outside their applicability domain, and the honest output is a wide interval plus an explicit out-of-domain warning -- which is far more useful than a fabricated point value. Thermodynamically, dG = RT ln(Kd) at T = 298 K with RT = 0.5924 kcal/mol; the two quantities must be derived from one another.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: [MAJOR] Developability and CMC are unassessed and the advertised "Copy FASTA -> Launch AlphaFold Server" workflow will emit invalid input: 11 of 25 sequences have odd cysteine counts, two contain the non-standard letter B, and one "sequence" is an English phrase — Three concrete defects, all of which are developability signals as well as software bugs. (1) app.js:381 sets sequence to the literal string "His14-Phe174-Linker-Peptide-Conjugate". This is not a sequence. The modal nevertheless renders a 3D backbone (app.js:674-773), a residue-level pLDDT curve (app.js:775-832) and a PAE heatmap (app.js:834-866) from it, because all three functions index into the string blindly; the pLDDT chart will produce axis labels like "H1 i2 s3 -4 15 44". The Copy FASTA button (app.js:660) will place this English phrase on the clipboard for submission to AlphaFold Server. (2) Two records (app.js:173, app.js:371) and one AF3 candidate (app.js:130) contain the letter B in "TCWWGBLCPFRRACPDCH". B is the IUPAC ambiguity code for Asx (Asp or Asn) and is not a synthesizable residue; AlphaFold Server rejects non-standard single-letter codes. (3) Eleven of the 25 sequences have an odd number of cysteines, including several with very high cysteine density -- 7 Cys in a 31-mer (app.js:173, 371), 7 Cys in a 37-mer (app.js:205, 361), 8 Cys in a 47-mer (app.js:143) and 8 in a 45-mer (app.js:215). An odd count guarantees at least one unpaired free thiol. Nowhere in the codebase is a disulfide connectivity specified, nor is oxidative folding, scrambling, dimerization, or thiol-mediated aggregation discussed. Consequence: The Copy-FASTA-and-launch-AlphaFold-Server workflow is one of the genuinely honest features of this platform, and these defects break it in exactly the cases a user is most likely to try. A user clicking Copy FASTA on AstroPafr-Block-A4 gets an English phrase; on AstroZo1-Protect-A3 or HippoWnt-FzdAgonist-X4 they get a string AlphaFold Server will reject. On the science side, the free-thiol problem is a real and underappreciated developability killer for cysteine-dense peptides: with 7 cysteines in a 31-mer there are 105 possible disulfide pairings for six of them plus a free thiol, so oxidative refolding yields a heterogeneous mixture rather than a single species. That mixture is not characterizable, not manufacturable to a specification, prone to intermolecular disulfide dimerization and aggregation on storage, and -- because aggregates are the dominant driver of anti-drug-antibody responses -- directly contradicts the unsupported "Immunogenicity: Low" labels at app.js:167, 271 and 303. None of this appears anywhere; the platform reports a single pLDDT and a single Kd as though a single, unambiguous molecule existed.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Required fix for DMPK-08: Add a validation function that runs over FULL_BRAIN_DRUGS_DATA and AF3_CANDIDATES at load time and rejects or visibly flags any sequence containing a character outside the 20 standard codes. Fix app.js:381 by supplying a real sequence or, if none exists, by rendering the card with an explicit "no sequence defined" state and disabling the 3D/pLDDT/PAE renderers and the Copy FASTA button for that record. Remove the B at app.js:130, 173 and 371 and replace with the intended D or N. For every cysteine-containing sequence, add an explicit disulfide-connectivity field and flag every odd cysteine count with a "FREE THIOL -- disulfide scrambling and dimerization risk" warning; for the 7-Cys and 8-Cys candidates, either specify the connectivity or reduce the cysteine count. Add a developability panel per candidate covering predicted solubility, predicted aggregation propensity, and Met/Trp oxidation and Asn-Gly deamidation liabilities, and remove the unsupported "Immunogenicity: Low / Very Low" strings at app.js:167, 271 and 303 in favour of "NOT ASSESSED".

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Ground truth for DMPK-08: AlphaFold Server accepts only the 20 standard single-letter amino-acid codes for protein chains; B, Z, J and X are rejected. For disulfide-containing peptides, the manufacturable design requires an even cysteine count with explicitly specified pairwise connectivity, a defined oxidative folding route, and demonstration of a single predominant regioisomer. Unpaired cysteines in a therapeutic peptide are conventionally either removed, substituted (to Ser or alpha-aminobutyric acid), or deliberately capped, precisely to prevent scrambling and thiol-mediated dimerization. Standard developability triage for peptides includes: sequence validation, disulfide connectivity assignment, predicted and measured solubility, predicted aggregation propensity, oxidation/deamidation liability scanning (Met, Trp, Asn-Gly, Asp-Pro), and an aggregation-linked immunogenicity risk assessment. The 25 sequences here are Trp-rich and several contain Asn-Gly, so oxidation and deamidation liabilities are present and unexamined.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Brain delivery of therapeutic proteins using an Fc fragment blood-brain barrier transport vehicle in mice and monkeys (2020). The Denali antibody transport vehicle (ATV): an engineered Fc fragment evolved to bind the apical domain of human transferrin receptor without amino acid insertions, deletions or unnatural appendages. A crystal structure confirms the TV binding site is distinct from the transferrin and FcRn sites. Anti-BACE1 ATV given peripherally to hTfR-knockin mice and cynomolgus monkeys produced substantially improved CNS uptake and sustained pharmacodynamic responses. The platform accommodates bispecifics and protein fusions. Application here: This is the concrete answer to what the 25 candidates are missing. Any of these peptide binders intended for a parenchymal CNS target must be reformatted as a fusion to a TfR1-binding transport vehicle rather than delivered as a naked peptide. It also supplies the correct experimental readouts the platform should be projecting -- brain uptake and target-engagement pharmacodynamics in an hTfR-knockin model -- instead of pLDDT and dG.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Delivery of the Brainshuttle amyloid-beta antibody fusion trontinemab to non-human primate brain and projected efficacious dose regimens in humans (2023). Roche's Brainshuttle module fused to gantenerumab. A single 10 mg/kg IV dose of trontinemab in NHP versus 20 mg/kg gantenerumab gave increased brain endothelial and parenchymal uptake with more homogeneous distribution; nonlinear mixed-effects PK modelling with correction for tissue residual blood estimated a 4-18-fold increase in brain exposure. A clinical PK/PD model of gantenerumab was extended with a brain compartment driving plaque removal, allometrically scaled from NHP, and used to predict first-in-human dosing. Application here: This is the exact template for the PK/PD layer this platform lacks: shuttle-enabled brain exposure, quantified fold-change with residual-blood correction, linked to a mechanistic brain-compartment PK/PD model, and used to project a human dose regimen. Building even a simplified version of this per candidate would convert DMPK-01 and DMPK-07 from blockers into a real deliverable.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Receptor-mediated drug delivery of bispecific therapeutic antibodies through the blood-brain barrier (2023). Quantitative brain-uptake benchmarks I verified directly in the full text: unmodified antibody uptake of 0.07 %ID/g (murine precursor of bapineuzumab) and 0.028 %ID/g (mAb158) in mouse; IgG in primate brain <0.01% of the plasma concentration; control mouse IgG2a brain VD of 11 uL/g, i.e. confined to the brain plasma volume. Against these, RMT-enabled molecules: chimeric HIRMAb 2.0 +/- 0.1 %ID/100 g in Rhesus at 2 h; cTfRMAb-AbetaScFv bispecific 3 %ID/g in mouse; 8D3 and RI7-217 TfR antibodies 3.1 +/- 0.4 and 1.6 +/- 0.2 %ID/g at 60 min. Reviews the TfR, insulin receptor, IGF1R and leptin receptor RMT systems. Application here: Supplies the hard numbers for the calibration argument in DMPK-02: the platform's 25 naked polypeptides will not exceed an unmodified IgG's 0.03-0.07 %ID/g, and the 20-100x gap to RMT-enabled molecules is the size of the problem the designs ignore. These are the reference values to display alongside any predicted brain exposure on the platform.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease and Blood-Brain Barrier Drug Delivery (2020). States that 98% of small-molecule drugs and ~100% of biologic drugs do not cross the BBB, and that in 2020 fewer than 1% of all Alzheimer's drug development projects incorporated a BBB delivery technology -- identifying the omission of delivery technology as a primary structural cause of AD drug-development failure. Application here: Directly diagnoses this platform's failure mode. CognitionBioChem is a well-executed instance of the >99% of AD programs that Pardridge identifies as lacking any BBB delivery technology. Citing it in the README would let the project position itself honestly relative to the field's known central obstacle rather than silently reproducing it.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Unbound Brain-to-Plasma Partition Coefficient, Kp,uu,brain -- A Game Changing Parameter for CNS Drug Discovery and Development (2022). A 47-question survey of DMPK organizations across major European and US pharmaceutical companies (Bayer, Vertex, Lundbeck, Biogen, AbbVie, Novartis, Janssen, Sanofi, Boehringer, Roche, Pfizer, AstraZeneca, GSK, Novo Nordisk). 93% report an established cross-disciplinary understanding of Kp,uu,brain; 79% describe its implementation as 'game-changing' for their portfolio; 74% consider the current toolbox for Kp,uu assessment and validation satisfactory for discovery and early development. Documents accepted methodology and its limitations. Application here: This is the authority for DMPK-07: Kp,uu,brain, not affinity and not total brain concentration, is the industry-standard CNS efficacy metric. It defines the minimum parameter set the platform must add (Kp,uu,brain, fu,plasma, fu,brain) and establishes that a CNS platform ranking on dG alone is out of step with essentially the entire industry.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: An AAV capsid reprogrammed to bind human transferrin receptor mediates brain-wide gene delivery (2024). BI-hTFR1, an engineered AAV capsid binding human TfR1, actively transported across human brain endothelial cells; 40-50x greater CNS reporter expression than AAV9 in human-TfR1 knockin mice, with the enhanced tropism CNS-specific and absent in wild-type mice. Delivery of GBA1 substantially increased brain and CSF glucocerebrosidase activity over AAV9. Application here: The state of the art for genetically encodable CNS payloads, and directly relevant to DMPK-05. Several of these designs are pure peptides that could in principle be expressed rather than infused, and the CNS-specific-versus-wild-type contrast is the cleanest published demonstration of what genuine mechanism-backed CNS targeting looks like -- the standard against which the platform's unmechanized region assignments should be judged.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Ultrasound Blood-Brain Barrier Opening and Aducanumab in Alzheimer's Disease (2024). Clinical demonstration in three participants of focused ultrasound applied with each of six monthly aducanumab infusions to transiently open the BBB in selected brain regions; Abeta reduction measured by F-18 florbetaben PET was numerically greater in insonated regions than in the contralateral homologous untreated regions, with safety and cognitive follow-up over 30-180 days. Application here: The only clinically demonstrated route to genuine region-selective enhancement of CNS drug delivery, and therefore the honest counterpoint to this platform's unmechanized 'five brain regions' claim (DMPK-05). If regional selectivity is central to the project's thesis, FUS is a real mechanism that could deliver it -- but it must be stated as the mechanism, with its own dosing and safety implications.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Discovery of Novel Blood-Brain Barrier Targets to Enhance Brain Uptake of Therapeutic Antibodies (2015). Transcriptomic and proteomic profiling of mouse brain endothelial cells identified basigin, Glut1 and CD98hc as highly abundant candidate RMT targets. Antibodies against each were significantly enriched in brain after in-vivo dosing; anti-CD98hc showed robust brain accumulation and a significant pharmacodynamic response measured as brain Abeta reduction. Also establishes the negative result that literature-nominated targets and microarray-identified BBB-enriched proteins failed to give meaningful uptake because of low protein abundance. Application here: Provides the second validated RMT pathway (CD98hc) as an alternative to TfR1, useful because TfR1 shuttles carry reticulocyte and iron-homeostasis liabilities. The negative-result half is equally instructive for this platform: target selection based on literature assertion rather than measured endothelial protein abundance produced no brain uptake -- exactly the failure mode of asserting cell-type targets without expression data.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Estimating peptide half-life in serum from tunable, sequence-related physicochemical properties (2021). A meta-analysis of 579 curated literature entries on peptide proteolytic lifetime, yielding a validated multivariable regression for human-serum terminal half-life of unmodified peptides: ln t1/2 = 2.226 + 0.053*(% nonpolar residues) - 1.515*(Trp present) + 1.290*(>=2 Tyr) - 1.052*(pI >= 10). Validated against a synthesized 16-peptide library spanning 7.4-403.4 min in human serum and against 21 clinical-stage peptides. Application here: I applied this model directly to all 24 parseable sequences to produce the predicted median 26-minute serum half-life in DMPK-06. It is transparent, sequence-only, requires no new data, and could be implemented in the platform in a few lines of JavaScript -- making it the cheapest possible first step toward an honest PK layer. Its coefficients also tell the designers what to change: reduce Trp, avoid pI >= 10, both of which these sequences violate systematically.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Therapeutic peptides: Historical perspectives, current development trends, and future directions (2017). Comprehensive review of the peptide therapeutic landscape from a curated dataset of peptides that have entered human clinical studies (>150 in active development, >60 approved in the US and other major markets), covering molecular characteristics, regulatory benchmarks, and therapeutic-area distribution. Application here: Establishes the realistic envelope for a synthetic peptide drug -- size, dose, route, and the stabilization chemistry that successful peptides carry -- against which these 25 unmodified 26-47-mers can be honestly benchmarked. Useful for DMPK-06 in choosing a specific half-life-extension strategy, and for setting a defensible upper bound on manufacturable daily dose.

source.ref: PMID 28236791; DOI 10.1016/j.colsurfb.2017.02.003; Colloids Surf B Biointerfaces 153:152-159

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Lipid selectivity in novel antimicrobial peptides: Implication on antimicrobial and hemolytic activity (2017). Two closely related designed peptides differing in hydrophobic moment and net charge: P6 showed no antimicrobial activity but high hemolytic activity, P6.2 showed good antibacterial and low hemolytic activity. Surface-pressure and zeta-potential measurements attribute the difference to relative affinity for zwitterionic PC (mammalian, erythrocyte-like) versus anionic PG membranes, and show P6's higher erythrocyte-membrane affinity drives its hemolysis. Application here: Modern demonstration that hemolytic liability in cationic amphipathic peptides is tunable by, and predictable from, hydrophobic moment and charge -- the two parameters I computed in DMPK-03. Supplies both the mechanistic rationale for flagging muH 0.88-0.89 at charge +5 to +9 as a hemolysis risk, and the experimental design (erythrocyte-membrane affinity plus HC50) that the platform must run before claiming '0% risk'.

tags: DMPK / CNS drug delivery (neuropharmacokinetics, peptide and biologic developability)
text: Peptide hydrophobicity controls the activity and selectivity of magainin 2 amide in interaction with membranes (1997). Magainin-2 amide analogues designed with varying hydrophobicity but deliberately conserved hydrophobic moment, net charge and hydrophilic-helix angle. Permeabilization of anionic PG vesicles was insensitive to hydrophobicity, whereas permeabilization of PC-rich (mammalian-like) vesicles increased sharply with it; antibacterial and hemolytic activity both increased with hydrophobicity, and a strong correlation was found between hemolytic effect and PC-vesicle permeabilization. Application here: The foundational controlled-variable experiment behind the hydrophobicity-hemolysis relationship used in DMPK-03. Older than the 10-year window but cited deliberately because it is the cleanest isolation of the causal variable, and because it directly refutes the platform's stated rationale at README.md:99 that hydrophobic peptide character protects against membrane-mediated toxicity -- in this class, hydrophobicity is the driver of mammalian membrane lysis, not a shield.
